posts.content:
We run agents across lead qualification, customer service, account routing, and many more areas at Personio. In addition to that, Personio employees have created countless smaller agents to help them automate part of their work using Claude, Langdock or n8n. That created a problem I don't think enough companies are talking about yet: how do you actually manage an agentic workforce?

A year ago, most of this didn't exist. Now that it does, three problems keep coming up.

→ Duplication is the first. Teams keep building agents that already exist somewhere else in the business, often less capable than one that's already running.

→ Governance is the second. When the person who built an agent leaves, ownership leaves with them, and nobody's sure who's keeping it updated. Especially as these agents are built across several platforms.

→ Cost is the third. It's hard to see what an agent actually spends in tokens, or whether it's earning that back. You essentially need to “performance manage your agents”

We think agents deserve the same operational discipline as any other business-critical system. I'm excited to share that we have built a platform that helps you manage your agentic workforce inside Personio, alongside your human workforce.

Every agent gets a clear owner just like a reporting line for humans, with handover built in when that person moves on. You can set up approval flows for new agents in the same way you'd use for a new hire. You can see what each team spends on agent costs next to the team's salary cost, and we'll flag it automatically when two agents are doing the same work. This allows you to use Personio to manage the challenges of a hybrid workforce, where agents support or amplify the work of humans.

If you want to bring order to your agentic workforce before it turns into a bigger problem, reach out. We're setting up our first customers on this now. 

https://lnkd.in/e7Kt-cFN

#AIatWork #FutureOfWork #HRTech

posts.content:
Germany's government adopted its Startup and Scaleup Strategy this week. Here's why it matters, and what needs to come next.

It's overdue, but 152 measures across eight action areas show Minister Katherina Reiche and the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy did serious work. The government is finally taking the ecosystem's concerns seriously.

Three things stand out:
→ Strengthening employee stock ownership. It’s one of the clearest levers for attracting and keeping top talent. I believe company success should be shared with everyone who contributes to it –  employees first. That's why at Personio we want all employees to be owners too.

→ Support for the 28th Regime (EU Inc.). A unified European legal framework makes cross-border scaling simpler. One vital step toward making Europe the best place to build and scale.

→ Consistent enforcement of the Digital Markets Act. Fair competition gives European startups and scaleups more room to grow.

What I want to see next: As Europe’s largest economy, Germany has the responsibility to lead on future technologies. Which means we need to move faster on AI, the biggest structural shift happening right now.

This cannot get lost in departmental responsibilities. It needs the highest political attention, the kind Macron has shown in France.

Judith Dada's "Europe 2031" scenario has generated real debate. The question isn't just about funding programs anymore. It's whether Europe shapes the global AI race or watches from the sidelines. Europe needs to build data centers fast, cut permitting from years to months, and team up with allies instead of going it alone.

The future of work belongs in that same conversation. The strategy talks about attracting international talent, and rightly so. But politics can't just watch while AI reshapes how companies are organized, how people and AI work together, what skills people need to build next. These questions are as important as capital access or regulation.

Thank you to the Startup-Verband for the work behind this. Your data and amplifying the ecosystem's voice made this strategy better.

TLDR: read and share the article linked below if you care about Europe's future 🇪🇺

AI is moving faster than most of us anticipated. The release of Anthropic's Fable 5 earlier this week is another proof for that.

At Personio, we're taking this seriously and investing heavily, both in how we operate internally and in the products and agents we're building for our customers to support them on their AI transformation. This is a defining moment and we're treating it as one, but the implications go well beyond technology.

What makes this moment different is the geopolitical dimension. The leading models are being built in the US and China, and so is the vast majority of compute to train and serve them. The next few years will be decisive when it comes to Europe’s future position in the world. We still have the potential to determine our own path, but that requires investment at a scale Europe hasn't attempted before, in energy, semiconductors, data infrastructure as well as drastic political reforms to actually deliver them.

That's why I'm sharing the #Europe2031 piece by Judith Dada, Daan Juijn, Stan van Baarsen, Philip Fox, Alex Petropoulos, and Michiel Bakker. It's a short scenario that paints a vivid picture of what's at stake for Europe over the next five years. Highly recommend reading, listening to it and sharing with others.

📖 Read the full article: https://europe2031.ai/
🎧 or listen here: https://lnkd.in/dB7gk5dj

Ursula von der Leyen and the European Commission's European technological sovereignty package is a welcome step forward. But if you read the scenario, it's clear we need to go further. 

I'm a strong believer that what's at stake here goes beyond competitiveness. If Europe loses control of the AI infrastructure underpinning its future economy, it loses the ability to make genuinely independent political decisions and to uphold our European values: human dignity, democratic freedom, and equality for all its citizens.

But zoom out and the picture looks different. AI is letting software companies create value for customers that simply weren't possible before. And it's compressing how long it takes to build and improve software. Both at the same time. That's a rare combination, and it's why we both left the conversation optimistic despite the noise.

Meeting Marc was also personally meaningful. Salesforce is the original cloud software company, and his book Behind the Cloud was one I kept coming back to when I was founding Personio. It shaped how I thought about building the company - including the idea to write the commitment to establish the Personio Foundation into the incorporation docs, which we set up in 2021 to support nonprofits working on education and climate.

We also talked about a new product that we are building to help customers with their AI transformation and I can't wait to share with our customers very soon.

The CEO of Goldman Sachs just wrote a great opinion piece in the NYTimes taking the other side of the pessimistic takes on AI and jobs. My bet is he’s right.

If you looked at what work looked like a few decades ago and saw how much faster everything is or easier it is to produce today - even before AI - you’d certainly have been convinced there’d be no jobs left. Yet the opposite has happened. Why?

What happens is we constantly just demand more from everything. Instead of automating a task and delivering the same value proposition, but cheaper, we just expect more from the overall product or service. Because some players in the market decides to do more with the automation, and it raises everyone’s expectations. So those that don’t respond can’t compete.

We get more financial analysis from analysts. We get much more comprehensive legal advice. We get more tailored financial services offerings. We get better software in niches we never thought we could automate. Our healthcare providers offer more tests and deeper medical advice. This just goes on and on. Those that don’t respond end up losing market share and dying off.

When you move from believing the world is static, you have a better view of how jobs evolve due to AI.

posts.content:
If your company uses AI anywhere in the employee lifecycle (hiring, screening, performance, promotions) there are three EU AI Act deadlines you need to know.

1️⃣ August 2nd is the transparency deadline: chatbots must say they're AI, deepfakes must be labeled. Important, but not the one that should be keeping HR teams up at night.

2️⃣ December 2027 is the most critical date for HR teams. That's when most standalone high-risk AI needs to be fully compliant. Recruitment tools, candidate screening, performance monitoring, promotion decisions. All of them. With documented risk management, bias-tested data, human oversight built in, and a conformity assessment you can show a regulator.

3️⃣ Then August 2028, for AI embedded in already-regulated products — medical devices, machinery. Same obligations but with one additional year to meet them.

December 2027 sounds distant. It isn't... not when you factor in inventorying which tools touch which decisions, running bias testing, building oversight processes, and documenting all of it. The companies that will struggle are the ones treating this as a project to start later.

At Personio, transparency and human oversight were already part of how we built before any of this was law. For us and the 16,000 SMEs we work with across Europe, compliance has never been a last-minute project.

#EUAIAct #HRTech #AICompliance #FutureOfWork #Personio

Our real‑time view across thousands of customers from all over Europe allows us to see market shifts as they start to happen. One very obvious trend to observe is headcount growth.

Across thousands of small and midsized organizations in Europe, the trend is clear: growth is still positive, but it has cooled steadily each year since 2022.
When you break it down, a few things stand out.

🌍 By market (second graph)
• Europe shows a similar overall slowdown, but each country follows its own path.
• Spain leads with a headcount growth of 9.9% in 2025, though far below its post‑COVID peak in 2022.
• The UK has slowed the most, reaching 2.7% in 2025 since peaking in 2022.

📊 By industry (third graph)
• Financial and Insurance companies have been the most resilient, still growing headcount at 13% in 2025.
• Manufacturing follows closely at 11%.
• Tech has seen the sharpest deceleration, moving from 27% in 2022 to 3.4% in 2025.

What is obvious: Since the end of zero interest rates, combined with economic shocks from tariffs and wars, most organizations have slowed headcount growth or even reduced their organizational size.

❓The big question is how AI will influence the coming years? Will we see large scale reductions as #LLMs automate big parts of people's jobs or will the productivity gains lead to higher economic output? How will the AI impact differ across different industries? Or will limitations in chip production or energy supply actually slow down the diffusion of AI and its impact over the coming years?

Nine months ago, we publicly committed to 2x the productivity of our R&D org at Intercom within 12 months.

It was a scary bet. Public accountability with no guarantee we'd pull it off.

We hit it with three months to spare. Looking back over 16 months, we've actually 3x'd - and I see no signs of plateauing.

Here's an honest look at what changed, with real data:

- PRs per person in R&D went from 16/month to 33/month 
- Product defect backlog down 54%
- Product changes more than doubled, shipping 39% faster
- Downtime from breaking changes DOWN 35%, even as deployments doubled
- Fully loaded cost per PR cut in half
- 93.6% of PRs are now agent-driven via Claude Code
- 19% of all merged PRs are now auto-approved by AI with zero human review

But the number that surprised me most:

1,100 of our 1,305 employees are now active Claude Code users. That's 600+ people outside of R&D - from finance, sales, legal, recruiting, hr etc - who are, for example, now building reports in minutes that used to take hours/days, or that simply weren't possible before.

The sentiment amongst many leaders is that AI tooling is becoming "too expensive." Our evidence suggests the opposite. Salary costs dominate every R&D org's spend. When AI leverage doubles your output, limiting token budgets is the expensive choice.

We're not done. The impact is still unevenly distributed across the team - our top 5% of engineers produce 6x the median output. There's huge latent potential. The biggest bottleneck now isn't technology, it's relearning how to work in the most effective way.

This is Part 1 - all the data, the nuance, what we measured and why, and what's still messy.

Part 2 is coming soon: the messy journey, how we actually did it, lessons learned, and what's next.

A few years ago, my coach Darren Gold recommended the book “Loving What Is” by @Byron Katie. It’s about a simple, yet difficult, concept: accepting things you cannot change so you don't waste energy fighting reality.

As an entrepreneur, I initially struggled with this. My whole career has been about proving that the "impossible" is possible. However, I’ve come to realize that when you accept reality as it is, you gain an entirely new perspective and discover additional possibilities. You find the power to extract positive outcomes from initially frustrating situations.

Applying this to the news today...

It is easy to get frustrated by the latest headlines or the daily tweets coming out of Washington. Like most of you, I would much prefer a US administration that cherishes long-term allies, respects sovereignty, and promotes the values of liberal democracies.

But, as I listened to European leaders over the last 24 hours, I found myself truly "Loving What Is".

For years, we have argued about the importance of European sovereignty - in our Economy, Technology, and Defense. We knew it was necessary to protect the European project and our values. But we were too preoccupied, too fearful, or simply not bold enough.

External pressure is the ultimate catalyst and so we should be thankful for them. This is our moment to stop reacting and start leading. Here is why:
• Economic Power: The EU is the world’s second-largest economy. Including the UK, Norway, and Switzerland, we are almost equal to the US.
• Scale: Our population is over 50% larger than the US.

There are many areas where we must catch up, but there is no reason to accept defeat.

I was encouraged to hear Ursula von der Leyen’s speech at #WEF in Davos yesterday on European independence. She even called out the #EUINC initiative from Andreas Klinger - a vital step toward strengthening our tech ecosystem and competitiveness.

There is much more to do on energy, defense, and trade. But I hope the events of recent weeks act as the needed catalyst for our leaders to 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐮𝐩 𝐛𝐨𝐥𝐝𝐥𝐲 𝐚𝐠𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐬𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐲 𝐛𝐮𝐥𝐥𝐲 - 𝐰𝐡𝐞𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐬𝐢𝐭 𝐢𝐧 𝐖𝐚𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐭𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐫 𝐌𝐨𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐰! As citizens, we must support our leaders in these urgent changes.

Both as a citizen and as CEO of Personio , I am proudly European. I will do whatever I can to support the transition to European independence. These are disturbing times, but they bring tremendous opportunities if we act with courage and resolve on what we can control.

Long live #Europe - from Nuuk to Kiew 🇪🇺

repost.content:
My personal 2025 wrapped - What Every European Must Know: For Europe, a small set of statistics influence what our continent will look like in 2050: how wealthy we are, who lives here, how much we can care for one another, and what kind of politics we get.

1. Growth: Bad - we're losing ground. Must reaccelerate.
2. AI: Now required to fuel growth. Need more.
3. Chips: Tough: Not a big enough footprint. Must increase.
4. Models: Tiny market share. Need more.
5. Investment: Widening gap to the US and in AI. Must step up game.
6. Adoption: Punching above our weight. Must double down. 
7. Electricity: Expensive and not enough supply. Need more. 
8. Migration: Early warning signs of brain drain: Need to attract best global talent and convince best European talent to stay.
9. Birth Rates: Low and unevenly distributed. Guarantees sustained migration pressure and deep demographic change. Must manage well.
10. Politics: Far-right surge. Risk of a vicious circle: Economic growth is no guarantee of social cohesion, but its absence is a recipe for social disaster. 

We need to fix the deep polarisation of Europe. To help this effort, we need to fix the economy. To do that we must win in AI. To do that we must fix energy, investment, and talent. 

So what is our silver lining? 

Despite the bleak averages, Europe is not a statistic. Summary statistics only allow limited conclusions about underlying individual data points. From “Swedes are taller on average than Italians” we cannot conclude that any particular Swede will be taller than any particular Italian. When pointing out that Europe is struggling in various critical dimensions, we cannot automatically deduce that therefore, it is impossible possible to achieve greatness in Europe. That is why we see great companies emerge even from the most unlikely of places. Greatness always has a way of defying the odds.

Pessimistic Euro-bashing is what a fixed mindset looks like in practice. A fixed mindset treats abilities and circumstances as largely innate and unchangeable; a growth mindset assumes they can be developed through effort and persistence.

As the saying goes: a small change in slope can make up for a lot of y-intercept. Even small shifts in direction now will compound into very different conditions a few decades from today. Europe is not unfixable in ten years. We are already seeing very encouraging signals in areas like AI adoption, initiatives like EU–INC and are hugely inspired by outliers like ElevenLabs Black Forest Labs Mistral AI Parloa poolside DeepL Lovable Isomorphic Labs Synthesia etc.

In the end, the statistics that scare us today are the sum of individual choices made yesterday. The statistics our children inherit tomorrow will be shaped by what we choose to do now.

As always, more on my Substack!

Michael Fritz is one of the most creative and impressive social entrepreneurs I've come across. He built Viva con Agua into a global movement for clean water access, never with the idea to just hope for donations, but instead build a business selling water and then funnel all profits into building wells that give people access to clean drinking water. 💦

His creativity has led to many new projects like #Goldeimer (selling toilet paper to build sanitary facilities) or the #MillerntorGallery (art fair generating profits for social causes). A few years ago he approached me (amongst others) to help fund his latest idea as an philanthropic investor: VILLA VIVA a social hotel that will generate profits on a new level that again can build wells and accelerate the impact of viva con aqua. The build was completed in central Hamburg in 2024 and it's been successful operating since. 🙌🏽

Last night I stayed there for the first time. 138 rooms, a rooftop bar, a restaurant, and 40% of all profits flowing to clean water and sanitation projects worldwide. Seeing Micha's vision come to life and hearing all the ideas he has for further expanding it is exciting.

What impresses me most is that Micha didn't stop at Hamburg. Cape Town also has a #VillaViva. Berlin is next. He's building the world's first social hotel chain!

📣Today, we are announcing both the #profitability milestone as well as the #acquisition of the AI agent startup aurio (acq. by Personio) which will contribute to our agentic roadmap at Personio to help deliver more value to our customers. 🚀

I’ve been thinking about what that actually means.

The last few years have been the hardest for Germany's economy since reunification. It shrank for two years in a row; something that hadn’t happened in over two decades. Also other European economies which we are active in have felt similar pressure. Industries that have defined this continent for generations have been under pressure. We were part of that reality. But while we continued to support our customers through this difficult phase, we als completed an internal transformation and I'm proud of the entire team for pulling that off.

What we’ve done in that time is more than survive a difficult market. We’ve completed a fundamental transition, from a venture-driven growth model to a sustainable software business that funds its own future and controls its destiny. Every major software company goes through this shift. What matters is how you come out the other side.

We’re coming out profitable. Growing. We can fund our innovation agenda from the strength of our business, giving customers confidence that we’re building for the long term. With 16,000 customers and an AI strategy that’s accelerating. As part of that I'm excited that the aurio team is joining us to build AI agents that help recruiting teams find the right candidates faster, while keeping hiring decisions firmly human-led.

Welcome, Aliosha, Johannes, Jakob and the aurio team. What you’ve built is impressive and it is no coincidence that many Personio customers had already chosen to accelerate their recruiting efforts with your product on top of the Personio ATS. I'm excited to make the aurio #screening and #sourcing agents available to all customers very soon, as well as the other #agents that are already on the roadmap.

Our mission is unlocking the power of people for organizations around the world. AI will pay a crucial role in helping us increase the impact we can have for our customers and profitability will ensure we own our own destiny and can deliver on this mission for decades to come.

This Sunday is the deadline for EU member states to implement the Pay Transparency Directive into national law. 22 of 27 are set to miss it — but the directive isn't going anywhere, and neither are the reporting obligations that follow.

→ Companies with 250+ employees must report their gender pay gap annually from June 2027, using this year's payroll data.
→ Companies with 150–249 employees report from 2027 too, but every three years.
→ Companies with 100–149 employees have until 2031.
None of these are soft deadlines, non-compliance carries real enforcement risk.

The EU's average gender pay gap is 11.1%, down from 13.0% in 2020 — but progress has stalled. Thirty years of policy hasn't moved the needle fast enough. Mandatory disclosure is the next lever.

That's why we built our Gender Pay Gap Reporting feature directly into Personio. It allows you to accurately report on employee pay, maintaining compliance in line with the directive and allowing you to immediately spot areas of opportunity.

For our 16,000 SME customers, it's ready to use today.

#GenderPayGap #EUPayTransparency #HRTech #Personio
